verdicts.argument: The contract does not contain a clause that merges or excludes the two listed positions, so the claim of duplicate billing cannot be substantiated.
No contractual provision demonstrates that the disposal position is covered elsewhere, thus the alleged duplication is unproven.
Without a specific clause linking the two positions, the claim of double remuneration lacks supporting evidence.
The contract does not provide a rule that would treat the frost protection positions as a single item, so the duplication argument fails.
There is no textual basis in the contract to consider the upper soil removal positions as one, therefore the claim is unsupported.
The specification does not require the missing asphalt class or compaction parameters, so the objection cannot be upheld.
The contract does not mandate the omitted paving dimensions or joint widths, thus the claim is not valid.
No clause merges the loading and hauling positions, so the alleged duplicate billing cannot be confirmed.
The contract does not contain a requirement for the missing asphalt class or compaction details, so the issue is irrelevant.
The contract does not specify a required landfill, therefore the lack of that detail does not constitute a breach.
Similarly, the contract does not demand landfill identification, so the claim cannot be sustained.
The contract does not prescribe concrete or exposure class for the shaft, so the missing information does not invalidate the bid.
